newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China insurer Pingan signs deal with McKinsey.
newsitem.headline: China insurer Pingan signs deal with McKinsey.

text.p: New York-based consulting firm McKinsey & Co Inc has signed a deal with China's Pingan Insurance Co to help the big state-owned insurer manage life insurance, growth strategies and human resources, the China Securities Bulletin said on Tuesday.
The 18-month contract was signed recently in China's southern boom city of Shenzhen where Pingan is based, the Hong Kong-based newsletter quoted a Pingan official as saying.
"McKinsey will help Pingan boost its international status, speed up growth and manage human resources," the official said. He did not give details.
Competition has become increasingly fierce in China's fledgling insurance industry as new foreign and domestic underwriters enter the once-restricted sector.
Pingan was China's second largest insurer in terms of premium income in 1996, capturing 14 percent of the domestic market, company officials have said.
The firm earned 10.5 billion yuan ($1.3 billion) in premium income in 1996, and Pingan officials said they hoped to boost that to 20 billion yuan this year.
Life insurance premiums accounted for about 7.0 billion yuan of Pingan's income and the company estimates that will rise to 13 billion yuan this year.
China's biggest insurance group is the state-run People's Insurance Company of China (Group), which once had a monopoly on the sector.
